findings.sourceEvidence: No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create, incur, assume or permit to exist any Lien on any property or asset now owned or hereafter acquired by it, or assign or sell any income or revenues (including Accounts) or rights in respect of any thereof, except: ...
findings.proposedIrEvidence: "action": "CREATE_LIEN" (rule r0, ir-rule:86a30550cb1333b4c723e64a) - the only action modeled for the entire §6.02 prohibition
findings.verifierReasoning: The operative source sentence prohibits two independently operative things: (1) creating/incurring/assuming/permitting to exist a Lien, and (2) assigning or selling any income or revenues (including Accounts) or rights in respect thereof. This second prohibition is a distinct anti-circumvention mechanism commonly used to prevent factoring/receivables-sale arrangements that achieve lien-like economics without creating a technical 'Lien'. The proposed IR models only a single action, CREATE_LIEN, for the entire section and never represents the assign/sell-revenue prohibition anywhere in the compilation, despite the same exceptions (a)-(i) applying to it. A hypothetical transaction where a Loan Party sells or assigns its accounts/revenue streams outside the enumerated exceptions would be prohibited by the real source text but would not be flagged as a violation under the proposed IR, since the IR contains no rule for that action at all. This is an omission of an independently operative rule, not merely an incomplete gloss on the Lien rule.

findings.sourceEvidence: No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create, incur, assume or permit to exist any Lien...
findings.verifierReasoning: The source text expressly extends the substantive prohibition to Restricted Subsidiaries (through the Loan Party's obligation not to 'permit' them to create Liens), meaning Restricted Subsidiaries are also functionally restrained from creating Liens absent an exception. The proposed IR's entityScope for the base prohibition lists only LOAN_PARTY, omitting RESTRICTED_SUBSIDIARY. If downstream compliance logic keys off entityScope to determine which entities' conduct is checked against this rule, a Lien created directly by a Restricted Subsidiary (rather than a Loan Party) could be missed as a scope match, producing a wrong compliance conclusion.

findings.sourceEvidence: any Lien on any property or asset of any Borrower or any Restricted Subsidiary existing on the date hereof and set forth in Schedule 6.02; provided that (i) such Lien shall not apply to any other property or asset of such Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary or any other Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary...
findings.verifierReasoning: Exception (c) explicitly applies to scheduled existing Liens on property of 'any Borrower or any Restricted Subsidiary,' not Borrowers alone. The proposed IR's entityScope for this exception rule is limited to BORROWER, which would incorrectly exclude a Restricted Subsidiary's pre-existing Schedule 6.02 Lien from qualifying for this basket under the IR, contrary to the source, which plainly permits such Liens for Restricted Subsidiaries too. This inconsistency is also visible when compared to sibling exception (d) in the same IR, which correctly uses the broader LOAN_PARTY scope.

findings.sourceEvidence: Liens of a collecting bank arising in the ordinary course of business under Section 4-210 of the UCC (or similar provision of the PPSA)...covering only the items being collected upon and banker's Liens and customary contractual rights of setoff arising in the ordinary course of business with respect to funds and securities in accounts...and not given in connection with the incurrence of Indebtedness
findings.proposedIrEvidence: conditions[0] (collecting bank Liens under UCC 4-210), conditions[1] (banker's Liens/setoff rights), conditions[2] (not given in connection with Indebtedness) all listed as separate items in the flat 'conditions' array of a single permission rule
findings.verifierReasoning: Clause (e) describes two disjunctive types of permitted Lien (collecting-bank Liens under UCC §4-210, OR banker's Liens/customary setoff rights), with the 'not given in connection with the incurrence of Indebtedness' qualifier most naturally attaching to the banker's-lien/setoff branch. The proposed IR lists all three as coordinate items in a single flat 'conditions' array on one permission rule. If the IR schema treats items in 'conditions' as conjunctively required (all must be satisfied), this would incorrectly require a Lien to simultaneously be both a UCC §4-210 collecting-bank Lien and a banker's Lien/setoff right, which the source does not require - they are alternative bases for the exception. This could alter a compliance conclusion where only one of the two lien types is present. The same structural pattern (potentially disjunctive sub-items flattened into one conditions list) also appears in exception (h) (customs Liens vs. inventory/bankers'-acceptance Liens), so this may be a recurring modeling issue rather than an isolated one; I cannot fully confirm from the given materials whether the IR's internal semantics treat 'conditions' as AND or OR, so I flag this as uncertain rather than certainly material.
